structure: tympanum (hidden tympanic annulus), diameter relative to eye diameter (TD/ED)
measurement: tympanum diameter 33.61% of eye diameter, holotype DHMECN 14454 (adult male)
method: taxonomic description of the preserved holotype; the percentage is printed in the Description of the holotype. Materials and methods > Morphological data and species descriptions lists 'tympanum diameter (TD (tympanum diameter)) and eye diameter (ED (eye diameter))' and says measures were taken with an electronic caliper; no separate operational definition of either is printed. Preservation as printed (Materials and methods > Specimen management): 'The specimens were fixed in formalin at 10% concentration and definitively preserved in 70% alcohol'.
conditions: One specimen. Holotype DHMECN 14454, adult male, Naturetrek Vizcaya Reserve, Tungurahua Province, Ecuador. Material examined prints paratypes DHMECN 14451 (male), 14452 (male), 14453 (juvenile) and 14550 (female) although the paratype heading says '(1 female, 3 males)'. The same sentence prints the tympanic membrane as undifferentiated from the surrounding skin and the annulus as visible beneath the skin, rounded and laterally orientated. Contrary or inconsistent statements in the paper: Diagnosis item (2) says 'tympanum absent, hidden beneath the skin; tympanic anulus visible under the skin measuring 25% of the eye diameter', which differs from the 33.61% of the holotype sentence; the Abstract says the species is characterised by not having a tympanum externally visible; Table 3 prints TD males 0.7-0.8 mm and female 1.0 mm against ED males 2.2-2.4 mm and female 2.6 mm. No external tympanum is visible, so this is a measurement of the hidden annulus region as the paper labels it. Anatomy only; hearing not tested.

structure: tympanum (tympanic membrane and annulus), diameter relative to eye diameter (TD/ED)

method: taxonomic description of the preserved holotype; the percentage is printed in the Description of the holotype. Materials and methods > Morphological data and species descriptions lists 'tympanum diameter (TD (tympanum diameter)) and eye diameter (ED (eye diameter))', measured with an electronic caliper; no separate operational definition. Preservation as printed (Materials and methods > Specimen management): 'The specimens were fixed in formalin at 10% concentration and definitively preserved in 70% alcohol'.
conditions: One specimen. Holotype DHMECN 14479, adult female. Paratypes as printed: DHMECN 14482 (female), 14447 (female), 14480 (male), 14478 (male), 14481 (male). The sentence also prints tympanum visible in dorsal view and laterally projected, a low rounded supratympanic fold, and three subconical postrictal tubercles. Inconsistencies in the paper, kept here so the value is not read as settled: Diagnosis item (2) prints 'tympanic membrane and annulus present, equivalent to 25% of the eye diameter' (against 35% here); the holotype measurement list prints eye diameter 4.7 and tympanum diameter 2.5 (mm), which gives about 53% by my arithmetic; Table 3 prints TD females 1.1-1.2 mm and males 0.9-1.0 mm against ED females 3.0-3.1 mm and males 2.3-2.4 mm. The 35% is the sentence value only. Anatomy only; hearing not tested.

structure: tympanic membrane and tympanic annulus (external ear), presence
measurement: tympanic membrane and tympanic annulus absent, holotype CORBIDI 18226 (adult male)
method: taxonomic description of the preserved holotype by external examination; the paper prints no tympanum measurement. Preservation as printed: 'Specimens were fixed and preserved in 70% ethanol.'
conditions: One specimen as the source of the sentence. Holotype CORBIDI 18226, adult male. Paratypes as printed: CORBIDI 18224 (female), MUBI 14654 (female), CORBIDI 18225 (male), MUBI 14655 (male); the Paratopotypes text says 'Four specimens' but lists five codes (reader count). The Diagnosis (item 2) and the Abstract state the same absence for the species ('lacking a distinct tympanic annulus, tympanic membrane'), and the Comparisons say it differs from B. flammiventris and B. gymnotis by lacking a tympanum; no contrary statement. A supratympanic fold is present, short and weak. Anatomy only; hearing not tested.
